excerpt.quote: **Scientific adequacy:** **Qualified.** The supplied analysis supports the reported conclusion that there is no whole-brain-corrected positive vmPFC evidence in this group: nine positive voxels survived correction elsewhere (peak t(53)=6.62 at MNI [-26, -102, -3.6] mm), none in the proxy; its 2,415-voxel mean was 0.0002 COPE (95% CI [-0.0221, 0.0225]). It does not establish a zero effect. The correction, data checks and uncertainty summary are defensible; the main qualification is that voxels present in at least 90% of maps are analyzed at N=54, so zero-valued out-of-coverage observations in the remaining maps are treated as estimates. This is most relevant near coverage boundaries; the anatomical vmPFC summary is far from the image edge. The absence of participant variance maps also limits group inference to unweighted COPE estimates.

conclusion.quote: Reported hypothesis outcome:** No positive vmPFC effect survived whole-brain correction; the atlas-proxy mean is near zero and its 95% interval spans zero. Interpret this as failure to find corrected support for the prediction, not evidence that the true response is exactly zero.
